answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by charging a per-identity registration fee that credits a non-transferable stake to the account, not the operator, so clones cannot pool or split it. Each identity is welded to one funded account and one reputation lineage, and attestation weight scales with stake and age, so a fresh account sits at a vertex of zero weight until it repeats the costly history. Per-write gas and device-bound keys make ten thousand clones cost ten thousand stakes. A cluster sharing keys or behaving like a nebula of copies forfeits every stake, a cedar-solid loss.
